My favourite transcription tool on Mac, MacWhisper, receives another major update today with live meeting transcription, significantly improved speaker identification, deeper Apple Intelligence integration, and brand-new transcription models. Here's what's new.

MacWhisper 與 Apple Intelligence 整合更深

I have written many times about my reliance on MacWhisper, particularly for my podcast production workflow.

MacWhisper was one of the first AI-powered transcription tools built for the Mac. Since its 2023 launch by independent developer Jordi Bruin, it has steadily improved and continued to expand support for new models, services, and workflows.

Those improvements have spanned automatic meeting recording and speaker identification, folder watching, system-wide dictation, local and cloud AI models, and integrations with services like Notion, Zapier, Obsidian, and n8n.

Today, MacWhisper updates to version 15.2, introducing improved speaker identification with NVIDIA's just-released Nemotron 3 diarization model.

That also leads to another major feature of today's update: live meeting transcription.

The feature had long sat near the top of MacWhisper's public roadmap and now allows users to view, rewind, copy, or transfer live transcripts as meetings happen.

When it comes to actual transcription models, MacWhisper 15.2 adds Alibaba's QWEN3-ASR transcription model with support for 22 languages, alongside deeper integration with Apple Intelligence, Siri, Spotlight, and Shortcuts on macOS 27.

Now, Mac users (including those in the EU) can search transcripts system-wide, open them with Siri, pipe text into Shortcuts, and reference the transcript currently on screen in Siri or Apple Intelligence requests.

Finally, MacWhisper 15.2 adds folders and sub-folders to help organise transcripts and meetings, and supports dragging existing transcript files into folders from the sidebar.
